newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-rail boss released from jail - report.
newsitem.headline: French ex-rail boss released from jail - report.

text.p: The former chairman of France's railway authority, Loik Le Floch-Prigent, was released from Paris' La Sante Prison late on Monday after nearly six months in preventive detention, a prison spokesman said.
In a second corruption case, jailed French businessman Pierre Botton was taken to hospital on Sunday after a failed suicide attempt, police in the southern city of Grasse said.
Botton was jailed in January to three and a half years in a political sleaze case in Lyon, France's second largest city.

Botton was accused of misappropriating 48.5 million francs ($9.3 million) from firms he controlled and paying the money to his father-in-law, Lyon mayor Michel Noir and Cannes mayor Michel Mouillot, to win influence and public works contracts.

Le Floch-Prigent, a longtime friend of French President Jacques Chirac, resigned in July as chairman of the SNCF state railways after being taken into custody on suspicion of abuse of corporate funds, receiving proceeds of fraud and issuing false information when he headed French oil giant Elf Aquitaine.
Investigating magistrate Eva Joly, who is leading the corruption probe, had earlier turned down three previous requests by his lawyers for his release.
Sources close to the investigation said his release followed a decision to begin cooperating with the judge, which he had previously refused to do.
Le Floch-Prigent was required to pay bail of 500,000 francs (about $100,000) and will remain under judicial control despite his release, France Info radio reported.
Under French law, the judge would have been required to release him next month in any case, due to time limits on preventive detention.
Some 15 other individuals have been placed formally under investigation in cases linked to Le Floch-Prigent's activities.
Much of the probe centres on his activities at Elf Aquitaine, where he served as chairman from 1989 until 1993.

In a memorandum published recently in the French weekly L'Express, he described Elf as an instrument of French diplomacy and espionage in Africa, where Paris maintains close ties with its many former colonies.
